hero.title: 12 Best Okonomiyaki in Hiroshima
hero.dek: Find Hiroshima's 12 best Reddit-backed Okonomiyaki, perfect for enjoying near your lodging after a day exploring the city.

intro.answerFirst: Hiroshima's okonomiyaki scene offers a range of experiences, with prices varying across establishments, but Nagataya is a highly recommended starting point. The classic preparations stand out as the most authentic, especially oyster okonomiyaki, a seasonal treat best enjoyed in autumn and winter.
body: Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki is nothing like the Osaka version. Instead of mixing everything into a batter, Hiroshima layers it — thin crepe, mountain of cabbage, pork belly, yakisoba noodles, egg — all built on a searing teppan griddle. The result is taller, noodlier, and arguably more satisfying.

Every visitor to Hiroshima wants to try it, but choosing where is the hard part. Okonomimura? Nagataya? That place the hotel receptionist recommends? We dug through years of Reddit threads to find the spots real travelers and Hiroshima locals actually recommend.

picks.name: Nagataya (長田屋)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Two minutes from Peace Memorial Park, with a 4.4 rating across 3,100+ Google reviews — Hiroshima's single most-recommended okonomiyaki shop for first-time visitors.
picks.whatToOrder: Hiroshima-style with soba noodles and oysters when in season (October to March).
picks.insiderTip: Lines build by 11:30am; arriving at opening (or after 2pm) is faster.

picks.name: Hassho (八昌)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A Yagenbori veteran with a 4.2 rating across 1,700+ reviews, considered by Hiroshima regulars one of the most refined of the older-generation okonomiyaki shops.
picks.whatToOrder: Hiroshima-style with soba and a special topping of squid or shrimp.
picks.insiderTip: Counter seats sit you closest to the teppan; reserve when possible.

picks.name: Okonomiyaki Lopez (ロペズ)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A Yokogawa shop with a 4.7 rating across 960+ reviews — among the highest-scored okonomiyaki addresses in the city — run by a Mexico-born chef who keeps the Hiroshima format strict.
picks.whatToOrder: Hiroshima-style with soba noodles, pork, and a fried egg on top.
picks.insiderTip: Yokogawa is a quick train stop from Hiroshima Station — easy combine.

picks.name: Micchan Sohonten (みっちゃん総本店)
picks.neighborhood: Multiple locations (Hatchobori flagship, Fukuya dept store)
picks.address: Multiple locations (Hatchobori flagship, Fukuya dept store)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Often credited as the originator of modern Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki in the post-war years. The Hatchobori flagship still draws long lines and remains a Hiroshima brand-name pilgrimage.
picks.whatToOrder: Hiroshima-style with soba and the Micchan special triple-pork topping.
picks.insiderTip: The Fukuya department-store branch has the same kitchen but shorter lines.

picks.name: Hassei (八誠)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A Funairi-cho neighbourhood shop with a longstanding local reputation for the more traditional, slower-cooked version of Hiroshima okonomiyaki.
picks.whatToOrder: Hiroshima-style with soba, plus oysters in season.
picks.insiderTip: A short tram ride west from the centre — combine with the Funairi-cho riverbank walk.

picks.name: Reichan (麗ちゃん)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Inside Hiroshima Station's ekie dining floor, this is the most convenient real-deal Hiroshima okonomiyaki for travellers about to catch a shinkansen.
picks.whatToOrder: Hiroshima-style with soba — the standard travel-friendly version.
picks.insiderTip: Right inside the station ticket gates; ideal as a final-meal stop.

picks.name: Okonomimura (お好み村)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A three-floor building of okonomiyaki stalls in Shintenchi — over 20 small kitchens stacked together. A 4.2 rating across 8,400+ reviews makes it the most-reviewed okonomiyaki experience in the city.
picks.whatToOrder: Pick any open stall on the second or third floor — they all run the same Hiroshima format.
picks.insiderTip: Different stalls have different specialties; ask at the entrance which is busy with locals tonight.

picks.name: Hiroki (ひろき)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A Funairi-cho counter shop frequently named by Hiroshima locals as one of the better hidden picks — quieter, tighter than the central names, with a tightly-controlled teppan.
picks.whatToOrder: Hiroshima-style with soba, plus the daily seasonal topping.
picks.insiderTip: Smaller than most on this list; reservations help on weekend evenings.

picks.name: Nagata-ya (ながた屋)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A separate shop near Hiroshima Station's south exit, often confused with the Peace Park Nagataya (different operation, same family lineage). 4.4 rating across more than 3,100 reviews.
picks.whatToOrder: Hiroshima-style with soba and a side miso soup.
picks.insiderTip: Easier to walk into than the Peace Park original; functionally similar bowl.

picks.name: Soranoniwa (空の庭)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A Naka-ku shop pricing slightly above the standard, with more elaborate Hiroshima-style variants and a quieter dining room than the famous-name addresses.
picks.whatToOrder: Premium Hiroshima-style with soba, oysters in season, and a seasonal vegetable topping.
picks.insiderTip: Pricier; book ahead for weekend dinner service.

picks.name: Ekohiiki (えこひいき)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A Naka-ku counter near Hondori popular with Hiroshima office workers, with a tighter menu and faster service than the destination shops.
picks.whatToOrder: Hiroshima-style with soba — the no-fail standard.
picks.insiderTip: Faster than Okonomimura at lunch; useful for a quick meal.

picks.name: Chinchikurin (ちんちくりん)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A Hiroshima-born chain with a 4.2 rating across 460+ reviews, doing reliable Hiroshima-style at multiple locations including Hondori and the station area.
picks.whatToOrder: Hiroshima-style with soba plus a side of chicken karaage.
picks.insiderTip: The chain is open later than most of the family-run shops.

faq.question: What is the best okonomiyaki restaurant in Hiroshima?
faq.answer: Based on Reddit consensus, Hassho (八昌) in Yagenbori is the most respected among locals and repeat visitors. Nagataya near the Peace Park is the most popular with tourists. Lopez is the cult favorite for its unique fusion twist. All three are excellent — it depends on your priority: tradition, convenience, or something different.

faq.question: What is the difference between Hiroshima-style and Osaka-style okonomiyaki?
faq.answer: Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki is layered — batter, cabbage, pork, and yakisoba noodles are stacked and cooked separately on the griddle, then assembled. Osaka-style mixes all ingredients into a batter before cooking. Hiroshima-style is larger, includes noodles, and has distinct layers you can see when it's cut.

faq.question: Is Okonomimura worth visiting?
faq.answer: Okonomimura is a multi-story building with ~25 okonomiyaki stalls. It's touristy but still serves good okonomiyaki. Reddit's consensus: it's convenient and fun for the experience, but you'll get better okonomiyaki at standalone shops like Hassho, Lopez, or Hassei. Go if you want variety and atmosphere; skip if you want the absolute best.

faq.question: How much does okonomiyaki cost in Hiroshima?
faq.answer: A standard Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki costs ¥800–¥1,200 ($5.50–$8 USD). Adding toppings like cheese, mochi, extra meat, or oysters can push it to ¥1,500. It's a filling, complete meal — one okonomiyaki is plenty for most people.

faq.question: Should I get soba or udon noodles in Hiroshima okonomiyaki?
faq.answer: Soba (thin yakisoba noodles) is the traditional default and what most shops recommend. Udon gives a chewier, heartier result. Reddit travelers generally prefer soba for the classic experience, but udon is worth trying if you want something different. Some shops also offer 'double noodles' (soba + udon).

faq.question: Do I need reservations for okonomiyaki in Hiroshima?
faq.answer: Most okonomiyaki shops don't take reservations — you queue up. Peak times (lunch 11:30–13:00, dinner 18:00–20:00) can mean 20–40 minute waits at popular spots like Nagataya and Hassho. Visit off-peak (14:00–17:00) for shorter lines. Hassei accepts phone reservations if you can call in Japanese.

faq.question: What is Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki and how is it different?
faq.answer: Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki is characterized by its distinct layered construction, often containing thin crepes, generous amounts of shredded cabbage, pork, fried noodles (soba or udon), and an egg, all drizzled with a savory sauce. Unlike Osaka-style where ingredients are mixed, Hiroshima's layers create unique textures and flavors in every bite. Many attribute its popularization to places like Micchan Sohonten.

faq.question: Is it necessary to make reservations for okonomiyaki restaurants in Hiroshima?
faq.answer: For most popular okonomiyaki restaurants in Hiroshima, especially legendary spots like Hassho or conveniently located ones like Nagataya, reservations are generally not accepted, and waiting in line is common. Some larger or more modern establishments, such as Soranoniwa, might offer reservations, so it's best to check individual restaurant policies if you prefer to avoid queues.

faq.question: Where can I find okonomiyaki near Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park?
faq.answer: The absolute closest and most highly-rated option near the Peace Memorial Park is Nagataya, just a 2-minute walk away. Another excellent choice within walking distance is Okonomimura, offering a multi-story experience with many stalls, giving you plenty of options right in the heart of the city.

faq.question: Are there vegetarian options for okonomiyaki in Hiroshima?
faq.answer: While traditional Hiroshima okonomiyaki typically includes pork, some restaurants may offer custom variations or vegetable-only options. It's advisable to ask specifically for "niku-nashi" (no meat) or "yasai-okonomiyaki" (vegetable okonomiyaki). Places like the larger Okonomimura might have stalls that are more accommodating to dietary requests.

faq.question: What's the best time to visit Okonomimura for the best experience?
faq.answer: Okonomimura can get very busy, especially during lunch (12-1 PM) and dinner (6-8 PM) peak hours, and on weekends. For a more relaxed experience with shorter wait times, try visiting during off-peak hours like late morning (around 11 AM) or mid-afternoon (2-5 PM). This allows for more time to wander and choose your favorite stall without the rush.

faq.question: What should I order at a Hiroshima okonomiyaki restaurant for a first-timer?
faq.answer: For a quintessential first-time experience, order the "soba niku-tama" (pork and egg with soba noodles) as this is the standard Hiroshima style. You can always add extra toppings like cheese, green onions, or local Hiroshima oysters if they're in season, which are particularly popular at places like Nagataya or Hassho.
